title: B2+ · L50 — Final integration: mixed challenge
description: Reto final B2+/C1: integra idioms, hedging, register, phrasal verbs, y discurso profesional en escenarios reales.

questions.prompt: En un board meeting, un director admite honestamente la posicion competitiva de la empresa: 'Frankly, we're playing catch-up on this front.'
questions.question: 'Playing catch-up' means:
options: Playing a children's game or sport.
Trying to match or reach competitors after falling behind.
Being significantly ahead of the market.
Taking a lunch or coffee break.
questions.explanation: 'Playing catch-up' = idiom para intentar alcanzar a alguien que va por delante, tipicamente competidor de mercado. Colocacion muy comun en business anglo: competencia, tech, market share, feature parity. 'Frankly' anade tono senior de honestidad brutal. Contrasta con 'leading the pack' (liderando) o 'ahead of the curve' (adelantados). Registro: business-strategic. Error hispano: interpretar literal como juego infantil. La metafora deportiva (atletismo, futbol) es intuitiva pero requiere reconocer el uso metaforico especifico de business.
examples: We've been playing catch-up in mobile since day one — the competition had a two-year head start. → confesion estrategica
AI-first competitors have us playing catch-up on every front right now. → analisis de mercado 2024+

questions.prompt: Un cliente pregunta si podras entregar el proyecto en el plazo original. Sabes que es dificil pero no imposible.
questions.question: Choose the best hedged answer that balances honesty with diplomacy:
options: No way, that's absolutely impossible.
It's tight, but with a bit of a stretch we could probably hit it.
Yes definitely 100%, no problem.
Maybe? Who knows what will happen?
questions.explanation: Hedging maduro triple: 'tight' (senal realista de dificultad), 'a bit of a stretch' (marca esfuerzo requerido), 'we could probably hit it' (compromiso hedged con probabilidad implicita). NO cierres puertas ('no way' es rude) ni prometas de mas ('100%' te compromete peligrosamente sin margen). 'Who knows' proyecta inseguridad amateur. Diplomacia + honestidad simultanea. Registro: profesional-senior, tipico de PM/consultant negociando expectativas. Error hispano cultural: cerrar en 'si o no' binario cuando el hedge maduro sirve mejor.
examples: It's a stretch, but doable with focus and no distractions. → hedge realista + condicion
I'd rather commit to something realistic than promise the moon and disappoint. → filosofia de commitment

questions.statement: 'To flesh out' an idea means to develop it in more detail with substance and depth.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Flesh out' (phrasal verb — metafora de anadir 'carne' al esqueleto de una idea) = desarrollar en detalle una idea, plan, concepto, personaje, argumento. Muy usado en product, strategy, writing, filmmaking. Registro: profesional-creativo. Colocaciones: 'flesh out the plan', 'flesh out the concept', 'flesh out the character', 'flesh out the details'. CUIDADO con false friend: 'flush out' (sacar/expulsar) es OTRO phrasal verb con significado distinto. Error hispano frecuente: confundir 'flesh' con 'flash' o 'flush'.
examples: The pitch is solid but we need to flesh out the go-to-market strategy. → next step tipico product
Let's flesh this out in a working session next week — bring your notes. → invitacion a deep dive

questions.prompt: En un feedback 1:1, tu manager te dice: 'I want you to take more ownership of the launch.'
questions.question: 'Take ownership' in this context means:
options: Purchase the product or company.
Take responsibility and lead as if the outcome were personally yours.
Be selfish and take credit for others' work.
Sign a legal contract of ownership.
questions.explanation: 'Take ownership' = asumir responsabilidad TOTAL, actuar como si el resultado dependiera de ti personalmente. Palabra clave en performance culture (Amazon Leadership Principles, high-agency companies). Diferente de 'being assigned' — es proactivo y va mas alla del scope explicito del rol. Antonimo: 'passing the buck' (echar la culpa) o 'not my job'. Registro: performance/leadership. Error hispano cultural: interpretar como agresivo o inapropiado (asumir mas que lo asignado) — en anglo corporate high-performance es lo mas valorado.
examples: The best ICs take ownership without waiting to be asked or given permission. → cultura high-agency
Take ownership of the outcome, not just the tasks assigned to you. → framing maduro

questions.text: To be honest, I think we're overthinking this — let's just ship the MVP and iterate based on real user feedback.
questions.explanation: Discurso founder/PM autentico con lean-startup cadence. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'to be honest' con enlazado /təbiˈɒnəst/; 'let's just' con /tsdʒ/ cluster asimilado /letsʌdʒʌst/; 'ship the MVP' — MVP se pronuncia letra por letra /ˌemviːˈpiː/; 'iterate based on' con enlazado. Vocabulario: 'overthinking' (verbo comun en tech), 'ship the MVP' (lanzar version minima viable), 'iterate based on real user feedback'. Registro: startup/tech decisive.
examples: Ship first, perfect later — we're overthinking this endlessly. → decision paralysis
Real user feedback beats internal debate every time — always. → mantra product

questions.prompt: Ejecutivo en TED-style talk hace un contraste retorico: 'This isn't a nice-to-have — it's a must-have.'
questions.question: The contrast 'nice-to-have vs must-have' distinguishes:
options: Cheap features versus expensive premium features.
Optional or desirable features versus essential requirements.
Fun features versus boring necessary ones.
New innovations versus outdated legacy features.
questions.explanation: 'Nice-to-have' vs 'must-have' es contraste product/priority core. Ayuda a cortar scope brutalmente: nice-to-have puede esperar (o eliminarse); must-have es no-go sin ello. Marca de PM disciplinado que sabe priorizar. Relacionado: MoSCoW framework (Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have). Registro: product management. Uso practico: en scope discussions preguntar 'is this nice-to-have or must-have?' fuerza decision. Error hispano cultural: querer todo — la disciplina de descartar nice-to-haves es lo que distingue senior PM.
examples: Kill every nice-to-have this sprint — must-haves only. Scope discipline. → decision brutal
Security is a must-have; the fancy animation is nice-to-have. → priority call clara

questions.prompt: Empareja cada idiom/expresion B2+ con su significado:

pairs.right: Volver a un tema mas tarde

questions.explanation: Idioms nucleares del business English C1. OJO CRUCIAL con 'table it': US = 'aparcar/posponer'; UK = OPUESTO = 'ponerlo en agenda para discutir'. Este false friend UK/US genera confusiones reales en reuniones internacionales — verifica el contexto. 'Boil the ocean' es critique tipico de estrategia demasiado ambiciosa. 'Get buy-in' es step politico obligado antes de shipping — sin buy-in, hasta el mejor proyecto muere. Registro: business ejecutivo. Todos ubicuos en cualquier corporate anglo.
examples: Focus on what moves the needle, not what looks busy on dashboards. → priority coaching
Let's not boil the ocean — pick one metric and go deep on it. → PM discipline

questions.target: Look, I'll be straight with you: the timeline is tight, the scope is fuzzy, and if we don't lock priorities by Friday, we're going to burn the team out.
questions.explanation: Discurso senior leader haciendo push-back real y directo. Estructura retorica magistral: 'Look' (assertion + attention grab) + 'straight with you' (frame de honestidad brutal) + trio de problemas paralelos ('tight timeline', 'fuzzy scope', 'burn out') + condicional urgente cerrando. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'Look —', tempo firme y grave, enfasis en los tres problemas. Contracciones: 'I'll', 'don't', 'we're' obligatorias. Registro: senior leadership, tipico de eng manager o PM lead protegiendo su equipo.
examples: Tight timeline + fuzzy scope + tired team = missed launch. Math is math. → sober assessment
If we don't lock scope, no amount of hustle will save this project. → real talk

questions.prompt: En feedback constructivo tu manager senala un patron comunicacional a mejorar: 'Your work is strong, but you tend to ___ people when they disagree.'
questions.question: Choose the phrasal verb that means 'dismiss or reject their input abruptly':
options: look up to (admire)
shut down (dismiss/reject)
hold on to (retain)
take after (resemble)
questions.explanation: 'Shut down' (people/ideas) = cerrar la conversacion, invalidar, rechazar sin engage. Feedback dificil pero comun en performance reviews. Los otros phrasal verbs no encajan: 'look up to' = admirar; 'hold on to' = mantener aferrado; 'take after' = parecerse a un familiar. Registro: HR/coaching feedback. Uso practico: 'shutting down' es habito comunicacional a corregir en high-agency ICs que a veces dismissean input junior. Error hispano: no distinguir phrasal verbs por semantica sutil.
examples: You shut down Sarah in the last review — people noticed and it hurt her. → feedback especifico
When you shut down disagreement, you shut down learning across the whole team. → coaching pesado

questions.statement: 'I'm not sure I follow' is a professional way to say 'I don't understand' without sounding lost or unprepared.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'I'm not sure I follow' es masterclass de diplomacia profesional: pones la duda del lado de ELLOS (no expresaron claro) sin acusarlos directamente. 'I don't understand' es honesto pero suena limitado o poco preparado. Diferencia sutil pero critica en meetings con superiores o clientes. Registro: profesional-diplomatico. Variantes maduras: 'can you walk me through that again?', 'help me understand', 'I'm missing the connection'. Error hispano: usar 'I don't understand' seco cuando existe alternativa mas elegante y menos comprometedora.
examples: Sorry, I'm not sure I follow — could you unpack that a bit? → hedge + peticion
Help me understand the connection between A and B — I want to make sure I've got it. → clarifying elegante

questions.prompt: Cierre de una presentation de earnings donde los numeros son espectaculares: 'The numbers speak for themselves.'
questions.question: This expression means:
options: The numbers are literally loud and audible.
The data makes the argument obvious without needing further explanation.
The report is short and concise.
The numbers are physically speaking.
questions.explanation: 'The numbers/results/facts speak for themselves' = idiom clasico para cerrar cuando la evidencia es tan clara que argumentar mas seria redundante. Muy usado en pitches, board meetings, closing arguments, earnings calls. Requiere que los numeros REALMENTE hablen — si no, suena arrogante o vacio. Registro: profesional-oratorio. Colocacion: siempre reflexiva ('for themselves' o 'for itself'). Uso retorico: dejar caer la frase + hacer pausa dramatica es tecnica de speakers profesionales. Error hispano: interpretar literal el 'speak'.
examples: 300% growth year on year — the numbers speak for themselves. → cierre triunfal
I could argue for another hour, but the data speaks for itself. → close efectivo con confianza

questions.text: Honestly, I'd rather we push the launch by two weeks than ship something we're not proud of.
questions.explanation: Discurso senior lead con conviction sobre calidad. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'I'd rather' se pronuncia como unidad /aɪdˈræðər/ (contraccion + weak form); 'push the launch' con /ʃðə/ cluster; 'we're not proud of' se funde /wɪərnɒtpraʊdəv/. Estructura clave: 'I'd rather X than Y' (estructura de preferencia hipotetica formal). Vocabulario: 'push the launch' (colocacion — posponer lanzamiento), 'ship something we're not proud of' (frame emocional/quality). Registro: senior product/eng leadership.
examples: Push the date, protect the quality — that's the trade-off worth making. → filosofia clara
I'd rather ship late than ship embarrassing. → craftsmanship principle

questions.prompt: Manager senior te aconseja durante reunion de mentoria: 'You need to pick your battles.'
questions.question: This advice means:
options: Fight aggressively with everyone all the time.
Choose carefully which issues are worth pushing back on.
Avoid all forms of conflict completely.
Purchase weapons for defense.
questions.explanation: 'Pick your battles' = idiom clave de senior wisdom: NO pelees por todo, elige donde el pushback vale la pena. Consejo estandar a juniors que discuten cada detalle sin priorizar. Balance entre integridad (algunas battles importan) y capital politico (no puedes gastarlo todo en cada meeting). Registro: coaching/mentorship. Variante mas dramatica: 'this isn't a hill worth dying on'. Error hispano cultural: en algunas culturas hispanas defender cada punto es signal de integridad — en anglo corporate el pick-your-battles es senal de madurez politica.
examples: You have to pick your battles — otherwise you burn credibility on small stuff. → coaching wisdom
This isn't a hill worth dying on — save your political capital. → variante mas dramatica

questions.statement: 'Let's touch base next week' is a common but slightly cliche way to say 'let's talk again next week'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Touch base' = idiom de negocios ubicuo (origen: baseball, tocar base). Sinonimo funcional de 'connect', 'catch up', 'sync', 'circle back'. Overusado hasta el punto de ser casi cliche corporate, pero sigue siendo natural y aceptable. Registro: corporate US, aceptado global. Alternativas mas frescas: 'let's sync next week', 'let's catch up Thursday', 'quick sync?'. Error hispano: no reconocer el idiom por literalidad; requiere entender uso metaforico de baseball naturalizado. Signal generacional: boomers lo usan mucho; Gen Z prefiere 'sync' o 'connect'.
examples: Let's touch base Friday to see where we are on this. → cliche pero funcional
Quick sync tomorrow? → alternativa moderna, menos corporate

questions.target: Alright — congrats on reaching the end of B2+. Honestly, this is the level where English stops being an obstacle and starts being a tool. Now go use it in the wild.
questions.explanation: Cierre motivacional B2+/C1 con cadencia natural. Estructura retorica master: 'Alright' (transicion + close attention), 'congrats' (informal contraccion), reframe potente ('stops being X, starts being Y'), imperativo de cierre ('use it in the wild'). Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'Alright —', tempo lento y calido, enfasis en 'tool' y 'in the wild'. Contracciones: apropiadas para cierre calido. Registro: mentorship, teacher-to-advanced-student. Milestone del alumno: idioma como HERRAMIENTA no como OBSTACULO — este es el shift mental clave de B2+ a C1.
examples: You've built the toolkit — now use it in real conversations. → transicion a practica
B2+ is where fluency stops being a goal and starts being a habit. → milestone framing
